programmes.duration: 4 semesters over 2 years (M1 + M2); the M2 alone is 2 semesters (1 academic semester + 1 internship semester); Bac+4 entry level for M2
programmes.credits: M2: 60 ECTS (S3: 30 ECTS and 350 h of teaching; S4: 30 ECTS internship per UVSQ page, while the Paris-Saclay catalogue lists the internship unit as 24 ECTS). M1 total not stated on the pages read.

programmes.entry_requirements: M1: bachelor-level degree equivalent in computer science, mathematics, physics or mechanics (35 places). M2: M1 CHPS (automatic admission for UVSQ M1 CHPS), or a scientific M1 / engineering school with parallel computing (architecture, algorithms, programming) and applied mathematics; selection on file otherwise.
programmes.structure_summary: Part of the national network of CHPS masters. The M1 mixes mathematics (numerical analysis, modelling) with HPC (parallel architectures, parallel programming, distributed algorithms, software engineering for HPC and AI). The M2 has a common core (multicore programming, hardware accelerators, performance evaluation, numerical programming, data/learning, continuum mechanics) followed by one of two tracks: IHPS (high-performance computing, compilers, code optimisation, quantum computing) or MSCHP (modelling and simulation, PDE discretisation, domain decomposition, model reduction). Strongly project-oriented, ending with a 5-6 month internship.

programmes.structure_summary: Joint ENSEIRB-MATMECA and Université de Bordeaux track combining HPC and data science. Five teaching units: architectures, languages and programming models (MPI, OpenMP, GPU, HPC tools on the training cluster); HPC and learning algorithmics (parallel algorithmics and scheduling, data analysis, dense numerical linear algebra); runtime, extraction and visualisation (scientific visualisation, big-data processing, efficient deep learning, a 3D programming or quantum option); application modules (HPC application project, in-situ processing, data mining); languages and engineering culture. Engineering degree includes three internships totalling 12 months.

programmes.structure_summary: Engineering degree in computer science and telecoms with a 'HPC et Big Data' parcours. S7 and S8 give the foundations (functional programming, concurrent systems and middleware, optimisation and operations research, OpenMP, advanced linear algebra with Krylov and sparse methods, PDE, numerical simulation project). S9 has five UE: distributed systems and security (including a Calcul Parallèle unit with MPI and an introduction to GPU programming), advanced statistical machine learning, High Performance Scientific Computing (parallel numerical algorithms and performance analysis), inverse problems, and an elective UE (cloud and big-data infrastructure, cloud strategy, quantum mechanics for computing, etc.). S10 is the final-year project.

programmes.notes: Toulouse has no standalone HPC master found; the HPC-oriented offer is the HPC et Big Data parcours of the ENSEEIHT engineering degree (Master-level). The search also showed a Mastère Spécialisé 'Ingénierie pour la Valorisation des Données Massives' (Bac+6, with a unit 'Calcul Haute performance et applications'), not read in detail. S9 descriptions of the mandatory UEs were read in full, so 0 for viz means they do not mention it; the S7/S8 sheets list titles only and the pages for the two 'Infrastructure for ...' electives are empty, hence null for sysadmin, scheduling, containers, ML systems and observability. Elective-based topics (cloud, bigdata, quantum) are scored 2 because a dedicated course names the theme, but they are optional. Page text is flagged 'indicatives et n'ont pas de valeur contractuelle'.
